narrativeProgression.description: Sneha explains that on heating, lead nitrate dissociates to form lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen.
Sneha mentions the necessary materials for the experiment.
Sneha begins the experiment by lighting the candle.
Sneha adds lead nitrate to a test tube using a spatula.
Sneha heats the lead nitrate in the test tube over a candle flame.
Sneha cautions the viewers to tilt the tube away from their face to avoid the fumes.
Sneha observes that heating lead nitrate produces a crackling sound along with brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide.
Sneha lights a wooden splint and introduces it into the test tube.
Sneha shows that the splint relights, indicating the evolution of oxygen.
Sneha blows off the splint and puts the test tube in a test tube rack.
Sneha concludes that heating lead nitrate results in the evolution of brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide and a crackling sound.
Sneha states that the relighting of the glowing splint signifies the evolution of oxygen and concludes that this is a decomposition reaction.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: you
Today, let us study the heating of lead nitrate in air.
On heating, lead nitrate dissociates to form lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.
To conduct this experiment, we need the following materials.
Spatula, test tubes, test tube holder, lead nitrate and candle.
We can also use spirit lamp.
Let us first light the candle.
Take a test tube and add one or two spatula of lead nitrate to it.
Now hold it with the help of a test tube holder and heat it over the flame.
Observe it carefully.
Care should be taken to keep the mouth of the test tube away from your face to avoid the
fumes.
On heating, lead nitrate produces a crackling sound along with the brown fumes of nitrogen
dioxide.
Let us burn the splinter and introduce this glowing splinter into the test tube.
The splinter gets realed again.
Because from this experiment, we infer that on heating lead nitrate, brown fumes of nitrogen
dioxide is evolved along with the crackling sound.
The fact that the glowing splinter gets realed indicates the evolution of oxygen.
Hence, it is a decomposition reaction.
